C09-M01-L04-F1.title: Where Indian law meets the lab's records
C09-M01-L04-F1.caption: Each stage of an evidence item's life, the instrument most relevant to it, and the lab record that instrument relies on.
C09-M01-L04-F1.alt: Table with columns Stage, Instrument and Record the lab must hold. Readiness (slate): CERT-In Directions 2022; retained logs and synchronised clocks. Search and seizure (blue): BNSS 2023, Sections 105 and 176; seizure list, video, receipt and photos. Acquisition and examination (green): lab practice under the IT Act framework; hash with algorithm, tool and version, notes. Expert opinion (violet): BSA expert opinion and IT Act Section 79A; method, limits, facts separated from opinion. Production in court (orange): BSA Section 63 and the Schedule certificate; Part A and Part B citing the acquisition hash.
rows: Hash and algorithm; tool, version; notes
BSA expert opinion; IT Act s. 79A
Method, limits; facts apart from opinion
Parts A and B citing the acquisition hash
C09-M01-L04-F1.note: The certificate's hash must be the hash recorded at acquisition, traceable through custody.

C09-M01-L04-F2.title: India's electronic-evidence framework before and after 1 July 2024
C09-M01-L04-F2.caption: The earlier provisions that older judgments and procedures cite, beside the provisions now in force.
C09-M01-L04-F2.alt: Two-column comparison with vs between them. Before 1 July 2024: Indian Evidence Act 1872; Section 65B certificate; CrPC 1973 for search and seizure; Anvar (2014) and Arjun Panditrao (2020) on the certificate; Section 65A special rules for electronic records. From 1 July 2024: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023; Section 63 with the Schedule certificate, Parts A and B; hash value and algorithm on the certificate; BNSS 2023 with audio-video recording of search and seizure; forensic expert at the scene for serious offences.
